title: Square isomorphism on bounded below derived categories
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$

with its specified natural isomorphism $\theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ of functors $\Ab(Y_{\Et})\to\Ab(X'_{\Et})$ between the sheaf-level inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (of the square only the equality $fg'=gf'$ enters, through $\theta_\square$). The inverse images are exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]; for each edge $u\in\{f,g,f',g'\}$ let $u^{-1}_D:D(V_{\Et})\to D(U_{\Et})$ be the functor on the derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induced by applying $u^{-1}$ termwise to cochain complexes, with its natural isomorphism $\beta_u:u^{-1}_D(QK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u^{-1}K^\bullet)$ for every complex $K^\bullet$ [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], $Q$ denoting the localization functors at the quasi-isomorphisms; and let $u^{-1}:\Dplus(V_{\Et})\to\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ be its restriction to the bounded below derived categories, the inverse image on $\Dplus$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image].

For a complex $K^\bullet$ of sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$ the termwise isomorphisms $\theta_{\square,K^r}$ commute with the differentials (naturality of $\theta_\square$) and form an isomorphism of complexes $\theta_{\square,K^\bullet}=(\theta_{\square,K^r})_r:f'^{-1}g^{-1}K^\bullet\to g'^{-1}f^{-1}K^\bullet$, natural in $K^\bullet$. Write

$$
 \beta_1:f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D(QK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{f'^{-1}_D\beta_g}f'^{-1}_DQ(g^{-1}K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta_{f'}}Q(f'^{-1}g^{-1}K^\bullet),\qquad
 \beta_2:g'^{-1}_Df^{-1}_D(QK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}_D\beta_f}g'^{-1}_DQ(f^{-1}K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta_{g'}}Q(g'^{-1}f^{-1}K^\bullet).
$$

Let $\theta^{D}_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}:f'^{-1}_D\circ g^{-1}_D\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}_D\circ f^{-1}_D$ (functors $D(Y_{\Et})\to D(X'_{\Et})$) be the unique natural transformation whose component at $QK^\bullet$ is

$$
 \beta_2^{-1}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,K^\bullet})\circ\beta_1\qquad\text{for every complex }K^\bullet\text{ on }Y_{\Et};
$$

it exists, is unique and is a natural isomorphism by the universal property of the localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2), applied to $L=Q$, $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms, $F_1=Q\circ(f'^{-1}g^{-1})$ and $F_2=Q\circ(g'^{-1}f^{-1})$ (termwise composites), $F_1'=f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D$, $F_2'=g'^{-1}_Df^{-1}_D$, $\phi_1=\beta_1$, $\phi_2=\beta_2$, and $\tau=Q\theta_{\square,-}$ (a natural isomorphism, so its lift is one; $F_1,F_2$ invert quasi-isomorphisms since they are isomorphic to functors $F_i'\circ Q$). The *derived square isomorphism*

$$
 \theta^D_\square:f'^{-1}\circ g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g'^{-1}\circ f^{-1}\qquad\text{of functors }\Dplus(Y_{\Et})\to\Dplus(X'_{\Et})
$$

is the restriction of $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ to the full subcategory $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$: its component at $K\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ is $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb},K}$, a morphism between objects of the full subcategory $\Dplus(X'_{\Et})$. In particular, for a bounded below complex $K^\bullet$, its component at $QK^\bullet$ is, after the identifications $\beta_1,\beta_2$, the class $Q\bigl((\theta_{\square,K^r})_r\bigr)$ of the termwise isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Checked against unit sk-def-exchange (the isomorphism f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_* ≅ g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_* 'induced by f∘g'=g∘f'') and Stacks 07A7/0D6D/0736. Rewrote the statement to name every ingredient and every claim: the derived functors are first taken on the unbounded D (lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, Mathlib mapDerivedCategory with its identification β_u: u^{-1}_D Q ≅ Q u^{-1}), the natural isomorphism is lifted along Q there by the reviewed Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property clause (2) (Localization.liftNatIso), and θ^D on D^+ is its restriction to the full subcategory, its inverse images on D^+ being restrictions (def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image). The old wording claimed uniqueness on D^+ from the components at QK^• with K^• bounded below only; that needs every object of D^+ to be isomorphic to such a QK^• (truncation), a claim with no node, and is not needed by the user def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange, so it was replaced by the restriction (which matches the source Lean: mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso is fullyFaithfulCancelRight of the D-level iso; Mathlib's DerivedCategory.Plus.Q is not yet known to be a localization). Added stmt_deps def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact (termwise functors invert quasi-isomorphisms), lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property. The sheaf-level θ_□ is the datum of def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square; that the termwise θ is a morphism of complexes is its naturality (written in the statement). No new nodes. Mathlib: the pinned Mathlib has no composition or NatTrans version of mapDerivedCategory and nothing on D^+; Loogle's newer Mathlib has Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and NatTrans.mapDerivedCategory on D only (recorded). Lean: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.pullbackSquareComparison (slopmaster2, MorphismDefs.lean:145-153, sorry-free by the sorry map) builds this isomorphism on D^+ for the coefficient category A from the composition isos upperStarPlusComp and the square's equality; its sheaf-level θ is the composite of the composition isomorphisms upperStarComp, a choice of θ_□ consistent with def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square.
